newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar to spend $14-15 bln on gas industry.
newsitem.headline: Qatar to spend $14-15 bln on gas industry.

text.p: Qatar plans to invest $14-15 billion over the next three years to develop its gas and industrial infrastructure, officials said on Tuesday.

"This investment will be in addition to the $11.5 billion which we have already spent or committed on liquefied natural gas (LNG) projects, and expanding chemical plants and a refinery," a Ministry of Energy and Industry official said.
"The new investments will also be in the gas sector but there will be greater emphasis on setting up value-added product facilities," he said.
Qatar, which relies heavily on oil, plans to raise the share of industry in its 38 billion riyal ($10.43 billion) gross national product (GNP) to about half by the year 2000.
Industrial output accounts for only 20 percent of the country's GNP while oil contributes 35 percent and the rest comes from the services and financial sectors.
Over the past three years the tiny state which controls the world's third largest reservoir of natural gas has invested heavily in diversifying its economy.

It spent $6 billion on Qatar Liquefied Gas Co (Qatargas) which went on stream late last year, $385 million on expanding the facilities at Qatar Petrochemical Co, $528 million at Qatar Fertilisers Co and $408 million at Messaieed Refinery.
Qatar is also spending $4.2 billion on a second LNG project -- the Ras Laffan LNG Co (Rasgas).

Officials said the new investments include a third LNG venture, Qatar-Enron LNG ($5 billion), Qatar Fuel Additives Co ($700 million), Qatar Vinyl Co ($500 million) and Qatar-Phillips ethylene cracker project ($750 million).
It also includes Qatar-Sasol -Phillips gas-to-liquid conversion project ($500 million), a condensates refinery ($500 million) and further expansion of Messaieed ($550 million).

Plans are also underway to add two trains at Rasgas to lift capacity to 10 million tonnes a year at a cost of $5 billion and set up Qatar Clean Energy Co to produce methanol and methyl tertiary butyl ether (MTBE) at $600 million after 2000.
